title: Ashish Yadav Wins Silver at World U20, Ends India's 10-Year Javelin Medal Wait
excerpt: The 19-year-old threw 74.09 meters to become only the second Indian after Neeraj Chopra to medal in javelin at the World U20 Championships.
body:
• Ashish Yadav won silver in men's javelin at the 2026 World Athletics U20 Championships in Eugene, Oregon, with a throw of 74.09 meters
  • He is only the second Indian to medal in javelin at the World U20 Championships, after Neeraj Chopra's gold in 2016
  • India's T. Dharanidharan finished sixth in the same final with a best throw of 72.35 meters

Ashish Yadav has etched his name alongside Neeraj Chopra's in Indian athletics history. The 19-year-old won a silver medal in the men's javelin throw at the 2026 World Athletics U20 Championships in Eugene, Oregon, ending India's 10-year wait for a javelin medal at the global junior competition.

Yadav's best throw of 74.09 meters came on his third attempt in the final on August 7, earning India's first medal of the championships. South Africa's Jan-Hendrik Heymans took gold with an enormous 80.50 meters on his sixth and final attempt — the season's world U20-leading mark. Dominica's Addison James claimed bronze with 73.89 meters, a national U20 record.

Following in Chopra's Footsteps

Chopra remains the only other Indian to have medaled in men's javelin at the World U20 Championships. In 2016 in Bydgoszcz, Poland, the future two-time Olympic medallist threw a stunning 86.48 meters to win gold — setting a world junior record that still stands a decade later.

"Ashish's podium finish ensures that India now has two medal-winning performances in the men's javelin event at the World U20 Championships."

— Times of India

While Yadav's 74.09 meters is well short of Chopra's record, the silver medal itself is significant. It confirms that India's javelin pipeline — largely inspired by Chopra's rise from junior world champion to Olympic gold medallist — is producing genuine contenders at the age-group level.

Two Indians in the Final

India had two finalists in the event. T. Dharanidharan finished sixth with a best throw of 72.35 meters on his fifth attempt, after qualifying for the final with 68.07 meters. Having two Indian javelin throwers reach the final of a world championship at any level is unprecedented and points to the depth developing in the event.

Other Indian Performances in Eugene

Mohommed Ashfaq produced another standout result on Day 3, breaking the men's U20 national record in the 400 meters. The 19-year-old clocked 45.81 seconds in his heat — second behind USA's Jayden DeLeon (45.63s) — to qualify for the semifinals. He bettered his own previous national record of 46.05 seconds set in April.

In women's discus, 18-year-old Amanat Kamboj finished sixth in the final with a personal best of 53.24 meters. Basant progressed to the men's high jump final after clearing 2.14 meters.

India's Javelin Program

The results at Eugene cap what has been a strong stretch for Indian javelin on the global stage. At the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow just days earlier, Neeraj Chopra and Yash Vir Singh delivered a historic double podium in the men's event.

India's javelin success is no longer a one-man story. From Chopra's 2016 junior gold to Yadav's 2026 junior silver, the discipline has expanded from a single talent into a genuine program with depth across age groups. For Indian athletics — long reliant on a handful of individual stars — that pipeline may be the most important takeaway from Eugene.

The 2026 World U20 Championships continue through August 9 in Eugene, with India's mixed 4x100 meter relay team among those still in contention.
